messages:
Anna (PM): quick sync — i'm drafting the PRD for committed capacity guarantees and need buy-in on degradation semantics + acceptance criteria before engineering review. propose we define: 1) committed throughput (tokens/s) per GPU tier, 2) soft latency envelope (p95/p99) under committed load, 3) explicit degradation modes and fallback routing, 4) test/acceptance checklist. link to draft: https://redwood.internal/docs/dedicated-guarantees-draft :eyes:
Mike (Eng - Runtime): +1 on needing concrete numbers. can we start with baseline for A100x8 and A100x4? also want clarity on whether guarantees are per-tenant or per-pool.
Sasha (Infra): per-pool is realistic for reserved pools. per-tenant maps to billing units but is harder to enforce at runtime.
David (Customer Eng): customers expect "guaranteed throughput" to mean predictable tail latency. they care most about p99 spikes during noisy neighbors. we should include a clause about priority isolation and burst allowances.
Anna (PM): good point David. proposed minimal guarantees: A100x8: 30k tokens/s committed, p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 380ms under sustained commit. A100x4: 15k tokens/s, p95 <= 260ms, p99 <= 480ms. open to engineering pushback.
Mike (Eng - Runtime): those latency targets look aggressive for long sequences. are these measured at 512 tokens avg? we need a defined profile. also we need to specify how batching affects these numbers and the target batch size distribution.
Priya (SRE): for SLO testing we need reproducible workload spec. suggest we use two profiles: short-chat (avg 64 tokens, 95% below 128), long-generation (avg 512 tokens). acceptance runs for both.
Jason (Product): add a requirement: graceful fallback policy when committed pool is saturated — prefer warm-compatible model variants with quantization to preserve response shape. customers should get explicit notification + incident link when fallbacks hit >5% of requests.
Anna (PM): here is a draft degradation policy snippet for the PRD:
```
# degradation_policy
- priority: committed
  if_pool_util >= 95% then
    - route_to: fallback_variant (quantized)
    - preserve_prompt_order: true
    - max_apdex_impact: 5%
    - notify: customer + incident
- if_region_unavailable then
    - route_to: cross-region-pool (best-effort)
```
Mike (Eng - Runtime): implementable, but we should replace hard 95% with a sliding window metric (5m avg) and add cooldowns to avoid flapping. also need to define compatibility constraints for fallback variants (max delta in logits / safety checks).
Sasha (Infra): ops question: do we allow burst above commit on best-effort? if yes, we must document throttling and billing implications.
David (Customer Eng): customers will expect a clear SLA table and a simple email/webhook that explains when fallbacks occurred. also include a rollback plan for model regressions caused by fallback variants.
Priya (SRE): acceptance criteria proposal: 1) load test harness shows p95/p99 within +/-10% of target for both profiles at committed throughput for 1h, 2) degradation triggers route to fallback <= 2% false positives during chaos tests, 3) observability: per-tenant metrics + alerting for >1% fallback in 15m.
Anna (PM): love those acceptance items. we also need an on-call runbook snippet for when fallback increases >10% in 30m — who owns rollback, who notifies legal/CS.
Jason (Product): suggest adding rollout criteria: canary on 5% of traffic for 48h, monitor latency, fallback rate, quality regressions via eval prompts. must be green before 100% enablement.
Mike (Eng - Runtime): dev note: we'll need API flags for customers to opt into strict isolation vs cost-optimized pooling. that affects routing policies.
Anna (PM): action items: @Mike to validate feasibility for the A100 numbers + propose sequence-length profiled numbers by EOD Tues; @Sasha to scope per-pool vs per-tenant enforcement and billing implications; @Priya to draft acceptance test harness and thresholds; @David to collect top 3 customer asks/concerns to include in PRD. i'll incorporate and push PRD for engineering review next week.
David (Customer Eng): i'll pull notes from last 3 enterprise calls and DM to Anna.
deploy-bot: scheduled docs snapshot created: https://redwood.internal/snapshots/1744208888-degrad-policy-v1
